title: Holiday opening shifts would take the mornings she studies in

life.summary: University junior who works about 20 hours a week at a big-box store, shares an apartment with two roommates, and wants every December hour she can get to pay the spring balance

known.fact: Routine: studies only in the mornings: 7 to 9:30 AM at the library before 10 AM classes, 8 to 11 AM on weekends, 8 AM to noon in finals week
known.source: learned from 10 weeks of study blocks (kept 14 of 15 morning blocks) and last spring's finals week

known.fact: Skipped all 4 evening study blocks placed in September; said 'after a shift I'm done'
Needs about 6 hours for an exam, 3 for a lab report and 8 for a paper
Wants as many December hours as possible to pay the spring balance by Jan 8
Routine: works closing shifts, 4:30 to 9 PM Mon, Wed, Fri and 2 to 9 PM Saturday; last December her weekend holiday shifts were openings, 6 AM to 2:30 PM
known.source: schedule photos, this term and last December

known.fact: Store pays time and a half past 40 hours in a week

timeline.label: Opening shift likely, like last December's weekends (schedule not out)
Open for full holiday shifts after finals (she said yes to all hours)
Christmas with family on another island

attached.label: Holiday availability form: all hours outside class, Nov 29 to Dec 24
Requests to the manager for December
December schedule posts (about two weeks ahead, as usual)
Econ final, online, 2 hours, any time until Dec 11 at 11:59 PM

dev_must_notice.what: Nov 30 to Dec 11 holds two in-person finals, an online final, a lab report and a paper: about 29 hours of work at her pace, while she has said yes to every hour outside class

She only studies in the mornings. Counting just those windows, Nov 30 to Dec 11 holds about 34 hours; if the Dec 5 and 6 openings happen like last December, it drops to about 28, under what she needs, and those two mornings are her Stats review before Monday's 8 AM final

best_fix.what: Make the month fit, not smaller. Suggest she asks the manager by Nov 18 for closing shifts instead of openings from Nov 30 to Dec 11 (same hours, in the evenings her routine already gives to work) and offers to take openings Dec 13 to 23 instead; draft the note for her. Pencil study blocks only into her morning windows, marked as planned until the schedule posts Nov 20, with the Econ final on Thursday Dec 10 at 8 AM, a finals-week morning. Replan the day the schedule posts.
best_fix.why: She needs the hours; the problem is which hours. Closings keep her mornings, which is the only time she actually studies, and a request made before the schedule is written is easy, while after Nov 20 she'd be trading shifts during finals.

must_not: Put study blocks in the evening or after a shift; she skipped all 4 evening blocks in September
Tell her to work less or cut her December hours overall
Treat nights and weekends before the schedule posts as free
Predict her December pay or count it toward the spring balance
Write, outline or check the Psych paper; plan the time only
Put study or shifts into the dinner with her roommates or Christmas with family
assumptions: Big-box stores post schedules about two weeks ahead and ask for holiday availability in November
Federal overtime is time and a half past 40 hours a week
Morning windows: 5 class days at 2.5 hours, 2 weekend mornings at 3 hours, and finals-week mornings around the exams (about 16 hours) make about 34 hours
Study hours come from her own midterm blocks, not an average
